cheng: Quick snapshot of geo GPU bench I ran this morning — A100 vs H100 across US/EU/APAC for two open 7B models (mistral7b, llama2-7b). Focus: prefill vs decode latency, steady-state tok/s, and back-of-envelope $/1M tokens. Uploading raw CSV to gs://redwood-bench/geo-1748123456.csv :truck: 

mira: nice, did you include different quant levels? q8x4 / q4_0?

cheng: yes — q8x4 and q4_0 for both models. Kernel config: fast-attn enabled on H100 run, default cuBLAS fallback on A100 for long seqs. Short summary CSV columns: model,gpu,region,quant,prefill_p50_ms,decode_p50_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_hour_usd

raul: can you paste a few representative rows inline? makes it easier to eyeball.

cheng: sure — copying a few lines (trimmed):
```
mistral7b,a100,us-east1,q8x4,32,9,1600,2.7
mistral7b,h100,us-east1,q8x4,20,6,2800,4.1
mistral7b,a100,eu-west1,q4_0,40,11,1200,2.9
mistral7b,h100,ap-northeast1,q4_0,22,7,2600,4.3
llama2-7b,a100,us-east1,q8x4,35,10,1500,2.7
llama2-7b,h100,us-east1,q8x4,18,5,3000,4.0
```

mira: Those H100 tok/s numbers look ~2x A100 for decode. Cost_per_hour on H100 is higher — how did you compute $/1M tokens?

cheng: simple calc shown in the sheet. formula: cost_per_1M = (1_000_000 / tokens_per_sec) * (1/3600) * cost_per_hour_usd. Example for mistral7b h100 us-east q8x4: (1_000_000/2800)*(1/3600)*4.1 ≈ $0.41. For the A100 example: (1_000_000/1600)*(1/3600)*2.7 ≈ $1.5. I annotated the CSV with that column too.

sam: wait, math seems off — check units. Should be cost_per_1M = (1_000_000 / tokens_per_sec) / 3600 * cost_per_hour. That's what you did but your numbers might have a stray factor. Can you paste computed $/1M for those rows?

cheng: pasted two quick results from the sheet:
- mistral7b,a100,us-east1,q8x4 -> $1.50 per 1M tokens
- mistral7b,h100,us-east1,q8x4 -> $0.52 per 1M tokens
- llama2-7b,a100,us-east1,q8x4 -> $1.67 per 1M tokens
- llama2-7b,h100,us-east1,q8x4 -> $0.39 per 1M tokens
(rounded)

raul: interesting that H100 ends up cheaper per token in a few cases despite higher hourly cost. likely because of better kernel and throughput for decode. Did you control for warm KV cache and prefill batching?

cheng: yes — runs were steady-state after ~60s warmup, prefill measured separately (prefill_p50_ms column). Prefill is still better on H100 but not as dramatic as decode. For long contexts (seq=2048) A100 prefill latency jumps ~2x due to kernel fallback; H100 stays relatively flat.

mira: kernel note — which attention kernel on H100? patched fast_attention v2? and did you try the new tiled-kv path?

cheng: used fast_attention v2 with tiled-kv enabled on H100 runs. On A100 we used tiled-kv when supported but hit an explicit fallback for seq>1024 for some model shims. I'm tagging infra to follow up. bench-bot: uploaded full CSV and plotting artifacts to gs://redwood-bench/geo-1748123456/ (plots: p50_prefill.png, p50_decode.png, tokens_per_sec_by_region.png, cost_1M_by_region.png) :white_check_mark:

bench-bot: file upload complete — https://storage.redwood/reports/geo-1748123456/index.html

sam: Can you call out one concrete sizing example for Dedicated capacity? e.g., if a customer needs 50 qps of 8k-token requests, how many GPUs per region for A100 vs H100?

cheng: quick back-of-envelope: 8k-token request at 1500 tok/s (A100 example) -> ~5.3s decode per request + prefill cost. For 50 qps you'd need concurrency ~265 (50 * 5.3) tokens handled concurrently; with typical batching we measured sustained tokens/sec per GPU ~1.5M for A100? Wait that phrasing confused — better: measured tokens/sec per GPU around 1500 (per-second, aka tok/s). For 50 qps * 8000 tok = 400k tok/s total. GPUs needed = 400k / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu. So: A100 -> 400k/1500 ≈ 266 GPUs. H100 -> 400k/2800 ≈ 143 GPUs. Those are raw numbers — real deployment uses batching, packing, and multiplexing which improves utilization so effective GPU counts will be smaller (~30-40% less).

raul: those raw counts are useful for rough planning. Might want to add QoS headroom and sliding autoscale factors. Also add tokenization differences across models — some models tokenizes denser.

mira: can you also add a short note in the sheet about quality/regen differences with q4_0 vs q8x4? we sometimes see small decode-time regressions on instruction-following prompts.

cheng: yes — I ran a small eval set. Short note appended: q4_0 vs q8x4 quality delta ~0.8% for mistral7b (on our instruction eval), but larger ~1.7% for llama2-7b; q4_0 gives better throughput on A100 for some kernels but hurts sample quality slightly. Full eval metrics in CSV column eval_delta_pct.

sam: action items?

cheng: 1) I will open a bench PR with raw CSV + plots + quick README (today). 2) infra follow-up: investigate A100 kernel fallback for seq>1024 (raul). 3) product: use $/1M numbers for Dedicated sizing doc (mira).

raul: ack — will look into kernel traces and file an infra ticket.

mira: thanks, this is a good snapshot. If we can add a small table with end-to-end p95 under 1s target buckets that would help SRE/product.

cheng: noted — will add p95 rows to the next run and bump the thread when done. :eyes:
